chapters.title: Knowledge Is Not Information
chapters.tease: Information is what you store. Knowledge is what you can act on within a minute.

chapters.title: The DIKW Ladder
chapters.tease: Each rung up the ladder has less volume and more value. Organising is the discipline of climbing.

chapters.title: Tacit Versus Explicit
chapters.tease: Most of what you know lives in your head. Writing concrete cases moves it where others can use it.

chapters.title: Findability Beats Storage
chapters.tease: A hoard you cannot search is a landfill. Every decision reduces to one question: will it be found?

chapters.title: The Cost of Organising
chapters.tease: You pay for organising at capture or at retrieval. Match the effort to how often you will look.

chapters.title: Everything Is a Collection
chapters.tease: Every collection faces four questions: selection, arrangement, access, departure. Trouble hides in the gaps.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Oath
chapters.tease: Preserve, describe, provide access. If a tool serves none of the three, it is decoration.

chapters.title: Entropy Is the Default
chapters.tease: No system stays organised on its own. A small weekly loop beats a brilliant one-off reorganisation.

chapters.title: Organise for the Question
chapters.tease: Sort things by how they will be asked for, not by what they are. The questions decide the shelf.

chapters.title: A Library Is an Argument
chapters.tease: Every arrangement is a claim about what matters. Make sure the argument your shelves make is yours.

chapters.title: Dewey and His Ghosts
chapters.tease: Dewey let shelves grow by giving each subject an address, then froze an 1870s worldview into them.

chapters.title: Faceted Classification
chapters.tease: Describe each item along several independent facets, and stop pretending it has only one home.

chapters.title: Tree Versus Graph
chapters.tease: Folders give each item one home. Links let it live in every context it belongs to. You need both.

chapters.title: Controlled Vocabulary
chapters.tease: Three synonym tags are three broken searches. Pick one preferred term and point everything else to it.

chapters.title: The Granularity Problem
chapters.tease: The right unit of knowledge is the smallest chunk that still makes complete sense standing alone.

chapters.title: Genus and Difference
chapters.tease: Define a term by its genus and its difference. If a definition excludes nothing, it is a mood.

chapters.title: Emergent Versus Imposed
chapters.tease: Impose the top layer where many must agree. Let the lower layers emerge, then promote what forms.

chapters.title: Polyhierarchy Is Honest
chapters.tease: A tomato is both fruit and vegetable. Give items one home and extra parents through tags or links.

chapters.title: The Miscellaneous Shelf
chapters.tease: Misc is your best diagnostic. When it passes a tenth of the collection, the categories are wrong.

chapters.title: Classification Is Power
chapters.tease: Whoever names the shelves decides what gets found. Neutral shelves do not exist; fair ones can be built.

chapters.title: The Name Is the Index
chapters.tease: The filename is the first and often only description anyone reads. Make it a one-line abstract.

chapters.title: Date-First Filenames
chapters.tease: Start filenames with year-month-day and your folder sorts itself into a timeline, for free.

chapters.title: Slugs, Not Sentences
chapters.tease: Lowercase words joined by hyphens survive every tool. Sentence-style names fail, rarely and painfully.

chapters.title: Frontmatter as Contract
chapters.tease: A few agreed header fields turn a folder of loose notes into a database, without running a database.

chapters.title: Provenance Fields
chapters.tease: Source, date, who and confidence. Without provenance, an estimate becomes a fact by the fourth copy.

chapters.title: Tag Hygiene
chapters.tease: Tags multiply silently. A monthly pass to merge, kill and split keeps search returning everything.

chapters.title: Status Over Folders
chapters.tease: Do not move files to show they are finished. Change one status word and break nothing.

chapters.title: The Permanent Identifier
chapters.tease: Give every important item an identifier that never changes. Links built on titles die at the first rename.

chapters.title: Metadata Is Not Free
chapters.tease: Every metadata field is a tax on every save. Keep the fields that answer real questions and stay true.

chapters.title: Naming as Thinking
chapters.tease: If you cannot name a document, you do not know what it is yet. That is a thinking problem.

chapters.title: Folders Versus Tags
chapters.tease: Folders answer where a thing lives. Tags answer what it is about. Use shallow folders plus good tags.

chapters.title: The PARA Method
chapters.tease: Sort by what you will do with it, not by what it is about: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive.

chapters.title: The Slip-Box
chapters.tease: One idea per note, a permanent ID for each, and a written reason for every link. That is the slip-box.

chapters.title: Depth Is Expensive
chapters.tease: Every folder level is a decision at save time and a guess at find time. Keep it to two or three.

chapters.title: Maps of Content
chapters.tease: Search tells you what exists. A curated map of content tells you what matters, and why.

chapters.title: The Inbox Pattern
chapters.tease: One place where everything lands unsorted, and a regular ritual that empties it. Both halves matter.

chapters.title: Notes Versus Wikis
chapters.tease: Notes record what was thought. Wikis promise what is true now. Do not let one pretend to be the other.

chapters.title: One Canonical Home
chapters.tease: Copies are fine. Confusion about which copy is true is not. Give each fact one owned home.

chapters.title: Structure Follows Team
chapters.tease: In a team, predictability beats cleverness. The best system is one a new hire can follow on day two.

chapters.title: The Self-Describing Folder
chapters.tease: A short README at the top of a folder answers six questions, so nobody has to ask you.

chapters.title: Capture Beats Curate
chapters.tease: An idea you never wrote down cannot be organised later. Catch everything first; decide what to keep later.

chapters.title: The Two-Second Rule
chapters.tease: If capture takes more than a couple of seconds to start, you will skip it exactly when it matters most.

chapters.title: Split Capture From Filing
chapters.tease: Noticing and deciding are different jobs. Capture raw at any moment, then file in batches later.

chapters.title: Progressive Summarisation
chapters.tease: Distil in layers, and only when you return to a note. Effort flows to what proves its worth.

chapters.title: Quote With Context
chapters.tease: A quote saved without its argument becomes a misquote within a year. Keep claim, reason, frame and stance.

chapters.title: Write Your Own Sentence
chapters.tease: A highlight is the author's thinking. A sentence in your own words is yours, and only yours gets used.

chapters.title: Capture the Question
chapters.tease: Save the question that made you look, not just the answer. Answers expire; questions keep.

chapters.title: Intake Rate Limits
chapters.tease: You can only process what you can review. Save faster than you read and you are building a debt.

chapters.title: The Source Ledger
chapters.tease: Keep one list of every source you follow, rated by how often it earned its place. Then cut the tail.

chapters.title: Capture as Commitment
chapters.tease: Every save is a small promise to your future self. Make only the promises you plan to keep.

chapters.title: Search Is a Skill
chapters.tease: Two words and hope is a wish, not a search. Phrases, exclusions, fields and dates make it precise.

chapters.title: The Inverted Index
chapters.tease: Search engines do not read your documents. They look up words in a list they made earlier.

chapters.title: Keyword Versus Semantic
chapters.tease: Keyword search finds exact strings, semantic finds nearby meanings. Each fails where the other works.

chapters.title: Recall Versus Precision
chapters.tease: Recall finds everything relevant; precision returns only the relevant. You cannot max both, so decide first.

chapters.title: Ranking Is Editorial
chapters.tease: Result order is a set of value judgements dressed as an algorithm. Choose them, or inherit somebody else's.

chapters.title: Browsing Still Wins
chapters.tease: Search finds what you can name. A well-ordered shelf shows you the thing next to it.

chapters.title: Serendipity by Design
chapters.tease: Random resurfacing, designed into your routine, turns old material into new thinking at almost no cost.

chapters.title: The Zero-Results Log
chapters.tease: Every search that finds nothing tells you exactly what is missing or misnamed. Log it, then fix it.

chapters.title: Chunking for Retrieval
chapters.tease: AI retrieval reads chunks, not documents. Cut on meaning, not on length, and every piece can answer alone.

chapters.title: Retrieval Is the Product
chapters.tease: Nobody experiences your taxonomy. They experience one moment: they found what they needed, or they did not.

chapters.title: The Forgetting Curve
chapters.tease: Memory decays steeply, then slowly. Review does not stop the forgetting curve, but it bends it.

chapters.title: Spaced Repetition
chapters.tease: Review each item just before you would forget it, and the gaps stretch from days to weeks to months.

chapters.title: Active Recall Wins
chapters.tease: Rereading feels productive and builds recognition. Recall from a blank page feels hard and builds memory.

chapters.title: Notes Are Not Memory
chapters.tease: A note stores the artefact, not the recall. If you cannot retrieve it unaided, you own a record of it.

chapters.title: The Generation Effect
chapters.tease: What you produce yourself, you remember. Copying borrows the words; rewriting them makes them yours.

chapters.title: Interleaving Topics
chapters.tease: Mixing topics within a session feels worse and works better, because you must pick the right tool each time.

chapters.title: Cues and Contexts
chapters.tease: Memory is retrieved by cues, not searched by content. Give each important fact a vivid hook.

chapters.title: Write to Remember
chapters.tease: Reading is renting, summarising is leasing, teaching is owning. Match the effort to how long you need it.

chapters.title: The Weekly Review
chapters.tease: One fixed hour a week to revisit, prune and connect is what turns a folder into a knowledge system.

chapters.title: Externalise Judgement Last
chapters.tease: Offload facts, dates and references freely. Keep taste, judgement and the questions in your head.

chapters.title: Weeding Is the Job
chapters.tease: Librarians remove books constantly. Courage to remove things is what keeps the remainder findable.

chapters.title: Knowledge Has a Half-Life
chapters.tease: All facts are true for a while. Proofs last centuries, prices months, status days. Label which is which.

chapters.title: The Review-By Date
chapters.tease: Give every time-bound fact a review-by date when you capture it, so the system raises its hand.

chapters.title: Dead Links Rot Quietly
chapters.tease: Links break without warning. If a source truly matters, archive the content, not just the address.

chapters.title: Duplicates Are Lies
chapters.tease: Two copies mean two versions of the truth, and at least one is wrong or soon will be.

chapters.title: Versioning Over Copies
chapters.tease: proposal-final-v3-REALfinal is a filing failure with a name. Keep one file and let history sit behind it.

chapters.title: Archive, Then Delete
chapters.tease: A cold archive gives you permission to clear the shelf. Once things prove nobody needs them, deleting is easy.

chapters.title: The Cost of Keeping
chapters.tease: Storage is cheap. Attention is not. Every item kept taxes every future search, browse and agent query.

chapters.title: Curation Is a Signal
chapters.tease: A short list someone maintained beats a long list someone generated. The value is the judgement.

chapters.title: Prune to Reveal
chapters.tease: Cutting is not loss, it is contrast. Halve a collection and the remaining half is finally visible.

chapters.title: RAG Is Cataloguing
chapters.tease: RAG is a library with a talkative front desk. The answer is only as good as the shelves behind it.

chapters.title: Embeddings as Shelf Space
chapters.tease: Embeddings shelve every text beside its neighbours in meaning. Nobody chose the shelves or can explain them.

chapters.title: Context Is the New Shelf
chapters.tease: A model knows two things: what it was trained on, and what is on its desk right now. Choose the desk.

chapters.title: The Agent Needs a Catalogue
chapters.tease: An agent with search and no map wanders. Give it an index note and its very first query improves.

chapters.title: The Memory File
chapters.tease: The memory file is the briefing for every first morning: read by the agent at the start of every session.

chapters.title: A README for Two Readers
chapters.tease: Every README now has two readers: a human who skims and an agent that believes every word.

chapters.title: Structured Beats Prose
chapters.tease: Models read prose well but tables more reliably. If a fact must be exact, store it in a structure.

chapters.title: Evaluate Retrieval Separately
chapters.tease: When an AI answer is wrong, check whether the right passage was ever retrieved before blaming the model.

chapters.title: Memory Needs Eviction
chapters.tease: An agent that remembers everything degrades. Promote what lasts, let the rest go, and evict what goes stale.

chapters.title: The Machine Reads Structure
chapters.tease: Every tidy convention you kept is machine-readable leverage. Tidy people built the ideal home for their tools.

chapters.title: Libraries That Watch Usage
chapters.tease: Log what gets retrieved and what never does. Usage data reorders shelves better than any taxonomy meeting.

chapters.title: Self-Organising Collections
chapters.tease: Embed, cluster and name: a taxonomy that emerges from what you actually collected, not what you planned.

chapters.title: The Interrogable Archive
chapters.tease: Not search, not chat: an archive you question in plain language that answers with sources you can check.

chapters.title: Personal Knowledge Graphs
chapters.tease: Give notes permanent IDs and reasoned links and your collection becomes a graph you can walk.

chapters.title: Shared Team Brains
chapters.tease: Team knowledge bases fail because contributing is harder than asking. Make the second explanation a link.

chapters.title: The Decision Log
chapters.tease: Decisions are the most valuable knowledge a team produces, and the why is almost always lost.

chapters.title: Provenance at Scale
chapters.tease: As synthetic text floods every corpus, knowing where a claim came from becomes the whole ballgame.

chapters.title: Knowledge as Infrastructure
chapters.tease: If your tools rely on your knowledge every day, run it like infrastructure: schemas, checks, backups, tests.

chapters.title: The Librarian as Agent
chapters.tease: Acquire, describe, shelve, retrieve, weed, answer: the librarian's verbs are an agent's job. Judgement is not.

chapters.title: A Library Is a Promise
chapters.tease: A library is a promise that things can be found again. Everything else is the machinery for keeping it.
